name: MimiClaw
vibe_summary: A bare-metal OpenClaw-style agent that runs entirely on a $5 ESP32-S3 chip — no Linux, no Node.js, just pure C. You talk to it over Telegram and it runs an LLM agent loop with local flash memory, sipping 0.5W of USB power.
best_for: Hobbyists wanting a $5 always-on AI gadget
Edge/embedded developers exploring LLM agents on MCUs
Users who want a low-power, local-data Telegram assistant
avoid_if: You need multi-channel support beyond Telegram/Feishu
You want a rich skill/plugin ecosystem
You are uncomfortable flashing firmware and managing ESP-IDF toolchains

0.5W power draw enables true 24/7 always-on operation
All data stored locally on device flash
Tiny pure-C codebase that is easy to audit

Requires cloud LLM APIs (Anthropic/OpenAI); no local model option
Constrained by ESP32-S3 memory and single-user design
Much smaller ecosystem, skills library, and community

overview_markdown:
MimiClaw is a bare-metal reimagining of the OpenClaw personal AI assistant, built to run entirely on a $5 ESP32-S3 microcontroller. Written in pure C on top of ESP-IDF, it eliminates Linux, Node.js, and any server infrastructure — the chip itself is the whole deployment. You message it via Telegram, and the onboard agent loop calls an LLM (Anthropic Claude or OpenAI GPT, switchable at runtime), invokes tools, reads from local flash memory, and replies, all while drawing roughly 0.5W from a USB port.

Its standout trait is persistence and frugality: memory survives reboots on SPIFFS flash, and the device can run 24/7 for pennies. Recent development is active, with fixes for group-chat mention filtering (to avoid burning tokens on unaddressed messages), SPIFFS filename limits, GPIO skill support, and CI releases shipping prebuilt firmware images. Compared to OpenClaw, MimiClaw trades the rich multi-channel gateway and skills ecosystem for radical minimalism — it is a single-user, single-chip appliance rather than a full assistant platform, and it still depends on cloud LLM APIs for inference.
